concepts.def: The amount of solute, in moles, dissolved in each 1 dm³ of solution. A solution labelled 0.500 mol/dm³ contains 0.500 mol of solute in every 1 dm³ of solution.

The solute is the substance that dissolves, the solvent is the liquid it dissolves in, and the solution is the mixture that results. Concentration in mol/dm³ uses the volume of the solution, not the volume of solvent that was added to it.
The unit used for amount of substance. The amount in moles of a substance of known mass is the mass in grams divided by the relative formula mass of that substance.
1 dm³ = 1000 cm³. A volume measured in cm³ is divided by 1000 to give the volume in dm³ before it is used with a concentration in mol/dm³.

concepts.term: Amount of solute in a given volume
concepts.def: amount in moles = concentration in mol/dm³ × volume in dm³. This gives the amount in moles of solute contained in the stated volume of solution.

concepts.term: Mass of solute in a given volume
concepts.def: The amount in moles of solute in the stated volume is found first from the concentration, then multiplied by the relative formula mass of the solute to give the mass in grams.

When two solutions react completely, the amount in moles of the solution of known concentration is found from its volume, converted using the mole ratio in the balanced equation, and then divided by the volume in dm³ of the other solution to give that solution's concentration.

concepts.term: Effect of mass and volume on concentration
concepts.def: Concentration in mol/dm³ rises when a greater mass of solute is dissolved in the same volume of solution, and falls when the same amount of solute is spread through a larger volume of solution, because concentration is amount of solute divided by volume of solution.

mcqs.q: A bottle of dilute hydrochloric acid is labelled 0.500 mol/dm³. What does this label tell you about the solution inside?
options: Every 1 dm³ of this solution contains 0.500 g of hydrogen chloride.
Every 1 cm³ of this solution holds 0.500 mol of hydrogen chloride.
Every 1 dm³ of this solution contains 0.500 mol of hydrogen chloride.
0.500 mol of hydrogen chloride was stirred into 1 dm³ of water.
mcqs.explain: A concentration in mol/dm³ states the amount of solute, in moles, present in each 1 dm³ of solution.

mcqs.q: Solution P contains 0.0400 mol of potassium hydroxide in 200 cm³ of solution. Solution Q contains 0.0400 mol of potassium hydroxide in 500 cm³ of solution. Which statement about their concentrations in mol/dm³ is correct?
options: P is the more concentrated, as the same amount of solute sits in less solution.
Q is the more concentrated, because it contains the larger volume of solution overall.
P and Q are equally concentrated, since each of them holds 0.0400 mol of solute.
Neither concentration can be found until the volume of water used is known.
mcqs.explain: Concentration is amount of solute divided by volume of solution, giving 0.200 mol/dm³ for P and 0.0800 mol/dm³ for Q.

mcqs.q: What amount, in moles, of sodium hydroxide is present in 250 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.200 mol/dm³?
mcqs.explain: amount in moles = concentration × volume in dm³ = 0.200 × 0.250 = 0.0500 mol.

mcqs.q: What mass of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in 200 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution of concentration 0.250 mol/dm³? (Relative formula mass of NaOH = 40)
mcqs.explain: amount in moles = 0.250 × 0.200 = 0.0500 mol, then mass = 0.0500 × 40 = 2.0 g.

mcqs.q: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution was neutralised by exactly 20.0 cm³ of hydrochloric acid of concentration 0.100 mol/dm³. NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O. What is the concentration of the sodium hydroxide solution?

In a titration, 20.0 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution was neutralised by exactly 25.0 cm³ of sulfuric acid of concentration 0.0500 mol/dm³. H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. What is the concentration of the sodium hydroxide solution?
4.0 g of sodium hydroxide is dissolved in water and the solution is made up to 250 cm³. What is the concentration of the solution in mol/dm³? (Relative formula mass of NaOH = 40)
mcqs.explain: amount in moles = 4.0 ÷ 40 = 0.100 mol, then concentration = 0.100 ÷ 0.250 = 0.400 mol/dm³.

mcqs.q: A student adds 250 cm³ of water to 250 cm³ of sodium chloride solution of concentration 0.800 mol/dm³ and stirs. What happens to the concentration, and why?
options: It stays at 0.800 mol/dm³, because no sodium chloride has been added to it or taken from it.
It doubles to 1.60 mol/dm³, because the volume of the solution has been doubled.
It cannot be worked out unless the mass in grams of dissolved solute is given.
It halves to 0.400 mol/dm³, because the same amount of solute is now in twice the volume.
mcqs.explain: The amount of sodium chloride is unchanged while the volume of solution doubles, and concentration is amount divided by volume.
